Previously, there were reports that Apple had shelved the long-rumoured all-glass iPhone, a device originally planned to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone's launch. According to Bloomberg, however, this redesign will still proceed as scheduled next year on the Pro models. Details below.

Bloomberg reports the redesign is on track

Earlier today, investment research firm Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating, citing its supply chain findings that Apple has abandoned a planned all-glass iPhone intended to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone.

A more recent Bloomberg report, however, states that the company "expects to launch iPhone Pro models with a new glass design next year," adding that "both the front and back of the device will use glass — internal code names V73 and V74 — with the material extending to the sides, and a metal frame running through the middle."

Nevertheless, the report also notes that the project has undergone adjustments since its original conception:

The report further directly refutes the earlier report from Jefferies, adding that "there has been no change to Apple's product roadmap."

Jefferies' claims

Earlier today, Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said that, based on the firm's supply chain checks, the all-glass iPhone had been cancelled due to poor production yields.

Lee described this development as a "significant setback" for Apple, noting that against the backdrop of rising memory costs, the cancellation could affect Apple's ability to push up prices and boost the average selling price and margins of its Pro models.

As a result, Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating and lowered the target price from US$285.56 to US$263.66. The previous target price cut was on 31 July, when it was reduced from US$308.92 following Apple's release of its fiscal third-quarter results for 2026 and its cautious guidance for the fourth quarter.
